title: Introduce interactive RAG authoring workspace + tiling/theme guide
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds a developer-facing Quickstart: an interactive RAG authoring workspace with layout tiles, theme tokens, and live preview. Useful for local authoring, debugging, and teaching teams how to tune retrieval/chain behavior. No API changes.
description:
Motivation: a lot of early users ask for a compact, local-first playground that demonstrates RAG authoring patterns (template prompting, tool bindings, and retrieval tuning) while also showing how to compose tiled UI panels (prompt editor, retrieval inspector, output preview, and telemetry console). This quickstart provides a small, fully documented workspace that teams can clone to learn and adapt UI+prompt ergonomics to their product.

What this PR does: introduces a new quickstart under quickstarts/interactive-workspace that contains: a React+Vite reference app, a small CSS tiling system and theme token file, an embeddable retrieval inspector component, examples of prompt templates with assertions, live streaming preview wired to the Redwood hosted API (configurable by env), and optional telemetry hooks that surface token/latency breakdowns. The description below lists changed files, a summary of commits, and the review log.

Key features: - Tile-based workspace with responsive stacking, keyboard shortcuts for panel focus, and accessible color tokens. - Theme tokens (light/dark/high-contrast) with a simple toggle and examples for customizing brand color, spacing, and font scale. - Retrieval inspector: shows top-K results, per-doc provenance links, and similarity scores (simulated for the quickstart via canned vectors). - Prompt authoring pane: parameterized templates and live sample inputs for testing reranking and tool calls. - Live preview panel: streams generation with prefix caching simulation to show cost/latency tradeoffs. - Telemetry console: token counts, per-request latency, and a minimal error histogram; can be turned off for air-gapped usage.

Testing & validation: - Unit tests for the theme utils and tile keyboard navigation. - E2E smoke (Playwright) that spins up the dev server and verifies: theme toggle persists, tile focus keyboard flows, and sample retrieval result appears. - Manual walkthrough documented in README with step-by-step expected outputs and a small prompt test-suite used by the QA harness.

How to run locally (short): 1) git clone && cd quickstarts/interactive-workspace 2) cp .env.example .env (set REDWOOD_API_KEY if you want live streaming) 3) npm install && npm run dev 4) open http://localhost:5173 and follow the onboarding tour in README.

Security/Privacy: the quickstart ships with canned vectors for offline mode; by default it does not persist any API keys and the telemetry hooks are opt-in. The README documents redaction advice when testing with real data.

Backward compatibility: none of the changes affect the Redwood API surface; this is purely a developer docs/quickstart addition.

Related Linear tickets: ENG-5829 (interactive workspace foundation), PM-194 (quickstart ship criteria).

notes_on_usage: The quickstart is intended for local experimentation and teaching — use OFFLINE_MODE=1 to run without network calls.
To switch themes programmatically, import theme/tokens and call setTheme('high-contrast') from the global helper.
Telemetry hooks emit a simple JSON payload to /telemetry when enabled; in prod, swap with your Kinesis/OTLP sink.
Examples include a small prompt-test-suite (prompts/*.json) used by the QA harness to detect regressions when tuning retrieval parameters.
